title: ClaimsExportV1
description: The `research-framework export --claims` envelope (issue #189): one claim record per qualifying vault note, plumbing skipped by the framework's own rules, citation credibility resolved the way the verifier resolves it. Produced by research-framework (`vault.claims_export`), consumed by downstream importers such as consumer_pipeline's `pipeline/vault_import.py`. Evolution follows ADR-0013: append-only within 1.x (additionalProperties stays true, new fields are optional), a new schema file per major, `schema_version` carried in the payload so a consumer can refuse a major it does not know. This schema is the consumer's floor; `tests/contracts/test_claims_export_schema.py` validates REAL producer output against it.

schema_version.description: `<major>.<minor>`. This schema accepts every 1.x payload and refuses any other major (ADR-0013 §2–§3).

kind.description: Discriminator, so a consumer holding several research-framework payloads can tell them apart before looking further.

version.description: The framework version that produced the export.

name.description: The vault folder's name; no personal data is derived from it.

corpus_dir.description: The corpus folder the claims were read from (`vault.corpus_dir`, default `data_vault`).

note_types.description: Note types the vault's spec declares; empty when the spec could not be read (see `warnings`).

quarantined.description: Claims in this export that come from `_pipeline/quarantine/` (0 unless `--include-quarantined`).

scaffold.description: Generator-owned files: the index trio, `_templates/`, any `_`-prefixed path.

exempt.description: `verifier_status: exempt` and `note_type: alias` redirect stubs — the verifier's own exemption rule.

malformed.description: Frontmatter the canonical codec refused; each one is also a `warnings[]` line.

missing_fields.description: No `type`, or an empty `summary` — nothing to claim.

warnings.description: Degradations the consumer should know about: unreadable spec, malformed notes. Never a reason the export failed — a failure is a non-zero exit, not a warning.

claims.description: Sorted by `id`, so two exports of the same vault diff cleanly.

id.description: Corpus-relative note path without its extension (`quarantine/<stem>` for a quarantined note). Stable across exports as long as the note is not moved.

note_path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, e.g. `data_vault/concepts/<note>.md`.

claim.description: The note's frontmatter `summary`, whitespace-normalised — the one-line claim the note supports.

note_type.description: The note's `type` as written. Mapping onto a consumer taxonomy is the consumer's job.

note_type_declared.description: Whether `note_type` is one the vault's spec declares; null when the spec could not be read.

verifier_status.description: `verified` / `pending` / `rejected` as the verifier stage wrote it; null when the note carries none.

template_version.description: The note-format template version the note was rendered from (spec 079).

support_count.description: Number of citations with a URL — `len(sources)`.

credibility_declared.description: The `credibility` the citation itself carries, verbatim; null when undeclared.

credibility.description: The effective level as the verifier resolves it (explicit → source default → catalog; COI-capped; off-field downgraded — spec 055/066/070). Null when nothing grounds the citation.

coi.description: The citation declared a conflict of interest.
